niche_preference_profile: Prefers polished, high-hierarchy interfaces that feel composed, intentional, and visually refined. They consistently like clear sectioning, concise copy, strong scanability, and layouts that feel complete rather than sparse or placeholder-like. Aesthetically, they often favor soft rounded cards, restrained but expressive color accents, and either calm premium minimalism or dramatic high-contrast dark treatments when those improve hierarchy and focus. They dislike clutter, fragmented onboarding mechanics, weak hierarchy, and screens where decorative elements or empty space reduce clarity or perceived substance.

criteria.description: Strongly prefers clearly separated sections/cards with an obvious headline-to-supporting-text hierarchy and minimal competition between content blocks.
Prefers quieter screens with fewer simultaneous focal points, less chrome, and less decorative or mechanical clutter.
Prefers interfaces that feel populated, complete, and functionally substantial rather than sparse, empty, or placeholder-like.
Prefers shorter headlines and tighter explanatory text with cleaner reading rhythm and less verbal clutter.
Prefers softly rounded, well-padded, visually refined cards or grouped modules with cohesive containment.
Prefers interfaces where primary actions and key messages are clearly emphasized through contrast, scale, and composition.
Prefers color used intentionally for hierarchy or semantics—muted/pastel accents in calm flows, but vivid accents when urgency or emphasis is needed.
Prefers interfaces that feel modern, curated, premium, and intentionally branded rather than generic, dated, or purely utilitarian.
Prefers color-coded or distinctive icons/avatars that add personality and semantic clarity over generic, repetitive, or purely functional icon treatments.
Prefers disciplined alignment, repeated row/section patterns, and steady vertical rhythm that make the interface feel systematic and composed.
